newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico same-day peso closes weak on speculation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico same-day peso closes weak on speculation.

text.p: Mexico's same-day peso recovered from early weakness but still closed 1.45 centavos off at 7.5790/7.5840 per dollar on Thursday due, traders said, to speculative dollar buying by local and foreign dealers.
"The market is very speculative. Foreigners are buying very heavily and that easily sways the domestic foreign exchange market," a trader said.
The still-trading benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart were meanwhile 1.45 and 1.4 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.5990/7.6035 and 7.5840/7.5990 per dollar.
Traders said that the partial recovery by the peso prior to the same-day market close was due to corporations selling dollars to take profits in pesos.
"It looks like someone stepped in to sell at 7.6250 per dollar...probably corporations who had held dollars for some time," a trader said.

The peso started to weaken on Wednesday, following a fall in primary interest rates, and was under further pressure from higher U.S. long bond rates on Thursday. Yields on the 30-year Treasury bond were up to 6.87 percent, from about 6.80 percent at midday Wednesday.
